Why would Cain name his son Enoch, such a weird name? That name sounds very familiar. The books bring it out: Cain’s Enoch has been identified with a fabulous king of the Babylonians, and the city Enoch with Erech. The Cainites, Cain’s descendants, dwelt in Enoch, or Erech. It was called Enoch first; later on Nimrod came over there, went to the same spot, and named it Erech, which is Iraq, which is Babylon.

Another book: though Cain represents the settled Sumerian people of Babylonia, he can yet be described as a fugitive and a vagabond. Half of an inscribed limestone tablet from the great temple of the sun in southern Babylonia, in the archaic writing of the oldest known period, mentions the town Adana or Nadu, which is Nod, Genesis 4:16. Nadu was a south Babylonian city. So the city Nimrod built in is the same place Cain resided in: Nadu is Nod, the land of Nod in which the city Enoch was built. Nod is southern Babylon, eastward of the garden of Eden.

“And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.” He resided in the land of Nod and built the city called Enoch, the wicked Enoch, after his son Enoch, the wicked son.

Bring it full circle: Cain was the king or ruler of Babylon in Genesis, and the white man is the ruler and king of Babylon now. The wicked ruled Babylon then, the wicked rule Babylon now. Nothing new under the sun.

Enoch is the same as Iraq that Nimrod built on top of.
